The tunnels of the Métropolitain railway of Paris (F. Bienvenüe, engineer-in-chief) under the two arms of the Seine, between Place Chatelêt and Place Saint Michel, were made by means of compressed-air caissons sunk beneath the river bed, were next made by the aid of temporary small caissons sunk through about 26 ft. of earth under the river.
